Title: LETTERS TO SITA
Author: Original excerpt, inspired by the premise of Sita Ramam (soldier + mystery pen-pal romance)
Draft date: 2026-09-03

EXT. ARMY OUTPOST - KASHMIR VALLEY - DAY

Snow-capped mountains ring a small army post. LIEUTENANT RAM, late twenties, stands guard at the gate, rifle slung over his shoulder, watching a convoy of villagers pass safely through a checkpoint he has just cleared of a mob.

A radio CRACKLES nearby. A JOURNALIST'S voice reports on the incident.

RAM
(quietly, to himself)
Just doing the job.

A young soldier, HAVILDAR ANWAR, jogs up holding a stack of letters.

ANWAR
Sir. The whole country's writing to you today.

He hands Ram the stack. Ram flips through them, unbothered, until one envelope stops him — plain, unsigned on the outside, in careful handwriting.

RAM
Who's this one from?

ANWAR
No idea. No return address.

INT. ARMY OUTPOST - BARRACKS - NIGHT

Ram sits on his bunk, lantern light flickering. He opens the plain envelope. A single page, elegant handwriting.

INSERT - THE LETTER

"They are calling you a hero on the radio. I only know you saved my brother without ever knowing his name. That felt like something worth writing about. - Sita"

RAM (V.O.)
(reading, half to himself)
Sita.

He turns the page over, looking for more. There isn't any. He sets it on the small shelf above his bunk, apart from the others.

INT. TRAIN COMPARTMENT - DAY

Weeks later. Ram, in civilian clothes, rides a crowded train south. Across the aisle, a young woman — SITA, MAHALAKSHMI, twenties, dressed simply, a dance bag at her feet — is arguing gently with a ticket inspector about a lost ticket stub.

Ram watches for a moment, then pulls the folded letter from his pocket and compares the handwriting on her ticket receipt without her noticing.

RAM
(to the inspector, stepping in)
It's fine. I saw her buy it at the platform counter myself.

The inspector, satisfied, moves on. Sita looks at Ram, surprised and a little suspicious.

SITA
You didn't see any such thing.

RAM
No. But you looked like you were about to miss your stop arguing about it.

She studies him for a moment — something familiar she can't place.

SITA
Do I know you?

RAM
(smiling, folding the letter back into his pocket)
Not yet.

The train rattles on. Neither looks away first.

INT. NOOR JAHAN PALACE - DANCE HALL - EVENING

Sita, in practice clothes, teaches a young PRINCESS the footwork of a classical dance, counting beats aloud. Ram waits near the doorway, uninvited, watching.

SITA
(not turning around)
You followed me from the station.

RAM
I asked for directions. Several times. To several places, all near here.

She finally turns, unable to hide a small smile.

SITA
And what would the letter-writer like to say, now that he's found his hero?

Ram takes out the letter one more time, holds it up.

RAM
That you write better than you argue with ticket inspectors.

SITA
(taking the letter back, gently)
Careful, Lieutenant. Letters are easier to be brave in than rooms.

She turns back to her student. Ram doesn't leave.

FADE OUT.
